properties.meta_title: Adventure Pass: Where to Buy, Prices & Digital Options (2026)
properties.meta_description: Buy a Southern California Adventure Pass: $5 daily or $30 annual. Find sellers by route, REI and Big 5 options, plus the San Bernardino digital day pass.
properties.card_summary: Where to buy a $5 daily or $30 annual Adventure Pass, with route-based sellers and a San Bernardino digital option.
properties.quick_answer: Need an Adventure Pass for your hike? A physical pass costs $5 daily or $30 annual for designated fee sites in four Southern California national forests. Buy from a listed seller before heading up, or check the San Bernardino digital day pass for that forest. A valid America the Beautiful interagency pass already covers Adventure Pass sites. Find sellers by route · REI & Big 5 · Order a physical pass · If stores are closed or sold out
properties.where_buy: Listed local vendors and Forest Service offices; REI or MyScenicDrives for physical passes. San Bernardino also offers a separate digital day pass.
properties.covers: Valid America the Beautiful interagency passes
properties.where_needed: Designated standard-amenity fee sites in the Angeles, Cleveland, Los Padres and San Bernardino national forests; check the exact site and posted signs.
properties.where_not: National, state, county and city parks; private properties; non-fee sites. Camping, wilderness permits and special-use fees may be separate.
properties.enforcement: Display your valid pass as instructed; failing to pay a required recreation fee can lead to a citation.

sections.heading: Where to buy an Adventure Pass near your route
sections.body: Choose a stop on your approach, rather than assuming the trailhead sells passes. These businesses are listed in the Forest Service vendor map, checked September 19, 2026. A listing confirms participation, not today’s stock or opening hours. Check with the seller before making a detour; ask specifically for a daily or annual pass. Route labels below are planning suggestions, not road-opening reports. Jump to Mt. Baldy · Azusa / East Fork · Big Bear · Crestline / Running Springs · Idyllwild.

sections.heading: Mt. Baldy Road: Icehouse Canyon and Manker Flats
sections.body: Mount Baldy Lodge — 6777 Mt Baldy Rd, Mt Baldy, CA 91759-9000. Listed for daily and annual passes. Directions. The Lodge is a business, not the Forest Service visitor center. Confirm sales hours before an early start. Buy the day before if your hike begins before it opens; a pass does not replace a wilderness permit or override a closure.

sections.heading: Azusa and East Fork Road
sections.body: Shell — 1195 W Foothill Blvd, Azusa, CA 91702. Listed for daily and annual passes. Directions. Camp Williams Café — 24210 E Fork Road #A, Azusa, CA 91702. Listed for daily passes only. Directions. Camp Williams is an East Fork Road stop; the Shell listing is in Azusa before the canyon approach. The vendor map lists only daily passes at Camp Williams, so check another listed seller if you want an annual.

sections.heading: Big Bear Lake: Village and town stops
sections.body: Big Bear Visitor Center — 40824 Big Bear Blvd, Big Bear Lake, CA 92315. Listed for daily and annual passes. Directions. The Visitor Center’s own page confirms daily and annual pass sales, cash or card, and published hours of 9am–5pm daily. Call 909-866-7000 to check availability or holiday changes. Big 5 Sporting Goods — 41385 Big Bear Blvd, Big Bear Lake, CA 92315. Listed for daily and annual passes. Directions.

sections.heading: Crestline and Running Springs approaches
sections.body: Lake Drive Hardware — 23895 Lake Drive, Crestline, CA 92325. Listed for daily and annual passes. Directions. Arrowbear Liquor and Deli — 32861 Hilltop Blvd, Running Springs, CA 92382. Listed for daily passes only. Directions. Choose the stop that fits your drive: Crestline for the Heart Rock approach, or Running Springs / Arrowbear along Highway 18. The Arrowbear listing is daily-only; do not assume it carries the annual pass.

sections.heading: Highway 243: Idyllwild and Humber Park
sections.body: Pine Cove Market — 23235 Hwy 243, Idyllwild, CA 92549. Listed for daily and annual passes. Directions. Shell — 26128 CA-243, Idyllwild-Pine Cove, CA 92549. Listed for daily passes only. Directions. Pine Cove is north of central Idyllwild on Highway 243. Choose a stop that fits your approach before continuing to Humber Park. A parking pass and any required wilderness permit are separate.

sections.heading: Does REI or Big 5 sell Adventure Passes?
sections.body: REI lists both versions: $5 daily Adventure Pass and $30 annual Adventure Pass. Select your store to check pickup availability, or check delivery timing before ordering. A product listing does not establish stock at every store. Big 5 has participating locations. The Forest Service lists its Big Bear Lake store above for daily and annual passes. Use the official vendor map to find other participating branches, then confirm with that branch. Do not assume every Big 5 has either pass in stock.

sections.heading: Need a pass today? San Bernardino’s digital day pass
sections.body: The official San Bernardino National Forest Day Use Pass is a separate digital option for that forest’s standard-amenity fee sites. Check the location, date, vehicle and current price on Recreation.gov before paying. Do not treat this forest-specific product as a four-forest Adventure Pass. It is tied to the selected date and vehicle and expires at 11:59pm that day. Recreation.gov recommends printing it when buying ahead; for an on-site purchase, compliance is checked by license plate. Buy before losing service and follow the display instructions. A valid interagency pass covers the same standard-amenity fees, so check what you already hold before buying. Neither pass guarantees a parking space or covers campground charges or separate permits.

sections.heading: Buy online: physical daily and annual passes
sections.body: The Forest Service links to MyScenicDrives for physical daily passes ($5) and physical annual passes ($30). REI also lists both. A shipped pass is not an instant download. MyScenicDrives’ delivery FAQ says its forest passes arrive by mail, cannot be printed, and cannot be replaced by an order receipt. Check shipping charges and the estimated arrival date at checkout. For a same-day trip, choose an in-person seller or an applicable official digital product instead.

sections.heading: If stores are closed or passes are sold out
sections.body: First, check whether you already have a valid America the Beautiful interagency pass. Otherwise, find a second seller in the Forest Service vendor map and confirm the pass type and hours before driving there. For San Bernardino fee sites, check the official digital day option. For another forest, use that forest’s official fee instructions; do not buy the San Bernardino product and assume it transfers. If you cannot obtain the required pass, choose a confirmed non-fee destination or change your plans. An order receipt, a closed shop or a full lot does not authorize parking.

sections.heading: Price, coverage and which pass you need
sections.body: The Forest Service’s Adventure Pass rules list the physical daily pass at $5 and the annual at $30, valid for 12 months from the purchase month. At those prices, six daily passes cost the same as one annual; the annual costs less starting with a seventh fee-paying day within its validity period. The pass covers designated standard-amenity fee sites in the Angeles, Cleveland, Los Padres and San Bernardino national forests. It is not required at every trailhead or roadside stop. Our list of where you need an Adventure Pass groups trailheads and day-use sites by the Forest Service’s fee listing. Check the destination’s fee notice and posted signs. Valid America the Beautiful interagency passes are accepted wherever the Adventure Pass is required; follow the instructions for your pass. National parks, California state parks, county and city parks, and private properties use their own fee systems. An Adventure Pass does not pay those charges or replace a separate wilderness permit. Check your trailhead parking guide and the official destination page before leaving.

faq.q: How much is an Adventure Pass?
faq.a: The physical Southern California Adventure Pass costs $5 daily or $30 annual. The annual is valid for 12 months from the purchase month. Online delivery charges may be extra. A valid America the Beautiful interagency pass also covers Adventure Pass sites.

faq.q: Where can I buy an Adventure Pass near me?
faq.a: Use the Forest Service vendor map and the route-based seller list above. Named options include Mount Baldy Lodge, Big Bear Visitor Center, Lake Drive Hardware in Crestline and Pine Cove Market near Idyllwild. Confirm opening hours and daily or annual stock before making a special trip.
REI lists the $5 daily and $30 annual physical Adventure Pass. Check the selected store’s pickup availability or the delivery estimate; the listing does not guarantee stock at every location.

Participating Big 5 branches appear in the Forest Service vendor map. The Big Bear Lake branch at 41385 Big Bear Blvd is listed for daily and annual passes. Confirm directly with your chosen branch before driving there.

faq.q: Can I buy an Adventure Pass online and use it today?
faq.a: A physical pass ordered from MyScenicDrives must arrive by mail; its order receipt is not a pass. San Bernardino National Forest separately offers an official digital day pass through Recreation.gov for its own fee sites. Check the exact forest, date and vehicle before buying.

faq.q: Does the San Bernardino digital day pass work in Angeles National Forest?
faq.a: Do not use the San Bernardino product for Angeles National Forest. It is forest-specific, unlike the physical four-forest Adventure Pass. Follow Angeles National Forest’s official fee instructions for your destination.

faq.q: Where do I buy an Adventure Pass for Mt. Baldy or Idyllwild?
faq.a: The Forest Service vendor map lists Mount Baldy Lodge at 6777 Mt Baldy Rd and Pine Cove Market at 23235 Hwy 243 near Idyllwild for daily and annual passes. Confirm sales hours and stock before leaving. These purchases do not replace a required wilderness permit.

faq.q: Is an Adventure Pass required at every Southern California trailhead?
faq.a: No. It applies at designated standard-amenity fee sites in the Angeles, Cleveland, Los Padres and San Bernardino national forests. Check your exact destination and posted fee signs. Other parks and private properties have separate rules.

properties.name: About TrailheadParking.com
properties.meta_title: About TrailheadParking.com: Who We Are & How Facts Get Verified
properties.meta_description: TrailheadParking.com covers the parking situation at trailheads across Southern California and the Utah national parks — lot sizes, fill times, passes, shuttles, closures — with every fact checked against official sources and date-stamped. From the makers of BigBearMap.com and LakeArrowheadMap.com.
properties.card_summary: Who runs this site, how facts get verified, and the sister guides it grew out of.

sections.heading: What this site is
sections.body:
TrailheadParking.com does one thing: it tells you what parking is actually like at mountain trailheads — how many cars fit, when the lot fills, what pass you need, what enforcement looks like, and what the realistic plan B is. It grew out of a pattern we kept seeing while building our area guides: the number-one thing that ruins a mountain day isn't the trail, it's arriving at 10am to a full lot with no plan.

Coverage spans four Southern California ranges — the San Bernardinos (Lake Arrowhead–Crestline–Running Springs, Big Bear, Forest Falls), the San Gabriels (Chantry Flat, Switzer Falls, East Fork, Icehouse Canyon), the San Jacintos (Idyllwild) and San Diego County (Cedar Creek Falls, Three Sisters Falls, Mt. Woodson, Torrey Pines) — plus Zion, Bryce Canyon and Arches, where shuttles, permit lotteries and reservation systems replace the usual question of lot size. We go where the parking question is genuinely confusing and the official answer is genuinely findable — the Park Service publishes lot-by-lot capacities that most forests simply don't.

sections.heading: How facts get verified
sections.body: Every fee, lot description, and access rule is checked against the official source — the Forest Service, the county, the operator — at the time the page is written, and every page carries a facts last verified date at the bottom. Mountain rules change seasonally, so perishable facts get re-checked on a recurring pass. When we get something wrong, we fix the page rather than defend it. No business pays to appear here and no placement is sponsored. Where something is genuinely uncertain — like the informal pullouts at the Arrowhead Pinnacles — the page says so plainly instead of faking precision.

sections.heading: The family of sites
sections.body: This site comes from the same maker as BigBearMap.com and LakeArrowheadMap.com — practical, verification-first guides to the San Bernardino mountain communities. The trailhead pages here link to those guides for the trails themselves; this site stays focused on the lot.

properties.meta_title: Where Do You Need an Adventure Pass? Fee Sites Map (2026)
properties.meta_description: Map and list of Forest Service trailheads and day-use sites in the Angeles, San Bernardino, Cleveland and Los Padres forests: which list an Adventure Pass fee, which list none, and which need a closer look.

sections.heading: How to read this list
sections.body: Adventure Pass site means the Forest Service lists a standard amenity fee there. In these four forests that fee is covered by a $5 daily or $30 annual Adventure Pass or a valid America the Beautiful interagency pass, displayed as instructed. Concession fee — pass acceptance varies means a concessionaire runs the site. Concession lots can sell their own parking pass. At Vincent Gap, the agency listing says Adventure Passes are honored, but the Big Pines concession lot did not accept them when we checked. Check the posted signs or the operator before relying on any pass. Records conflict — check first means the Forest Service record contradicts itself: it says no fee is charged but lists a $5 daily or $30 annual fee, or the reverse. We don't pick a side. Other fee type means the record names a fee that isn't the standard amenity fee, such as a special recreation permit or an expanded amenity fee. Don't assume an Adventure Pass covers it. Fee listed — type not stated means the record says a fee is charged without saying whether it is the Adventure Pass amenity fee, a permit (Cedar Creek Falls uses a Recreation.gov permit) or something else. No fee listed means the agency record lists no fee. That does not cover wilderness permits, campground fees or a nearby lot run by someone else.

sections.heading: Open and closed status
sections.body: A few sites carry a Forest Service "closed" flag, and we show it. We don't show "open", because these records can contradict a closure order. Echo Mountain Picnic Area and Inspiration Point on Mt. Lowe are listed as open, yet both are inside Angeles National Forest closure order 05-01-26-04 (Eaton Fire), which ran through December 31, 2027 when we checked on August 1, 2026. Those rows carry a warning. Each forest publishes its own closure orders, and roads can close separately, so check both before you drive.

sections.heading: Where we've checked a site ourselves
sections.body: When one of our trailhead guides covers the same place as a listed site, it appears in the "Our verified guide" column with its own fee answer and verification date. When the two disagree, the guide reflects what we found on our last check, and the agency listing is shown so you can see the difference. A guide that is merely nearby is linked as "Nearby, not this site", without its fee answer, because a lot a few hundred meters away can have different rules.

properties.card_summary: Which San Gabriel trailheads are closed under the Eaton Fire order, which are open, and where the official sources disagree.
properties.quick_answer: The Altadena front country is closed; most other San Gabriel trailheads we cover are open. Angeles National Forest order 05-01-26-04 closes the Sam Merrill, Echo Mountain, Mount Lowe, Idlehour and Castle Canyon trails and the Mount Wilson Toll Road below Henninger Flats through December 31, 2027. Eaton Canyon Natural Area, below the forest, is a county park that L.A. County lists as closed until further notice; its trails alert puts the trail's closure at December 31, 2027. Chantry Flat, Switzer, East Fork and Icehouse Canyon were all marked open by the Forest Service when we checked on October 17, 2026. Roads are a separate question: Caltrans has Highway 2 closed between Newcomb's Ranch and Vincent Gulch, and Highway 39 closed north of Crystal Lake Road. Trailhead by trailhead · What the order closes · Roads and other orders · Where sources disagree
properties.order: Angeles National Forest Forest Order 05-01-26-04, Eaton Fire Area Closure
properties.closed_trails: Sam Merrill (lower, middle, upper), Echo Mountain, Mount Lowe West, Mount Lowe (East), Idlehour, Castle Canyon
properties.closed_roads: Mount Wilson Toll Road below the Mt. Wilson Trail and below Henninger Flats; the Henninger Flats spur
properties.penalty: Up to $5,000 and six months in jail for an individual

sections.heading: Trailhead by trailhead
sections.body: Status as of October 17, 2026, from the Forest Service page for each site unless noted. "Open" here means the agency lists the site as open. It says nothing about whether the road up is open that morning or whether the lot has space. Echo Mountain and the Sam Merrill Trail (Altadena): closed. All three Sam Merrill segments, the Echo Mountain Trail and both Mount Lowe trails are on the order's closed list. That covers the climb from Lake Avenue and Loma Alta Drive and the route on to Inspiration Point. Echo Mountain parking guide Eaton Canyon Natural Area (Pasadena/Altadena): closed by L.A. County. The natural area, nature center and parking lot are county land outside the national forest. The county's park page reads "closed until further notice due to the Eaton Fire" (L.A. County Parks), and its trails alert lists the Eaton Canyon Trail and waterfall closed until December 31, 2027. The canyon above it, inside the forest, is in the federal closure area. Eaton Canyon parking guide Mount Wilson Toll Road and Henninger Flats: closed. The order closes the toll road below the Mt. Wilson Trail junction and below Henninger Flats, plus the Henninger Flats spur, so the Altadena gate on Pinecrest Drive is not a way in. Mt. Wilson Trail (Sierra Madre): sources disagree. The order does not list this trail as closed; it forms the closure's eastern edge, and L.A. County's trails alert lists it as reopened by Sierra Madre. The Forest Service's Chantry Flat page, however, lists the "Sierra Madre section of Mt Wilson Trail closed below Upper Winter Creek Trail." Until those agree, call the Sierra Madre Police Department at (626) 355-1414, which the city lists for trail closure information. Mt. Wilson Trail parking guide Chantry Flat (Big Santa Anita Canyon): open, with a road caveat. The Forest Service lists the picnic area open, day use 6am to 8pm, and names First Water, Sturtevant, the Gabrielino Trail and both Winter Creek trails as open. It asks hikers to stay off the Zion Trail for now, because post-fire flood damage still needs volunteer work. The road up can close for safety even while all of that is open; Sierra Madre controls the gate and L.A. County maintains most of the road (Forest Service). Chantry Flat parking guide Switzer Picnic Site (Switzer Falls): open. Listed open, day use 6am to 10pm. It sits on the open western stretch of Angeles Crest Highway, well short of the Highway 2 closure (Forest Service). Switzer parking guide East Fork (Bridge to Nowhere): open. Listed open 24 hours. East Fork Road leaves Highway 39 south of the Crystal Lake closure, so that closure does not block it (Forest Service). East Fork parking guide Icehouse Canyon (Mt. Baldy): open. Listed open. The free wilderness permit for the Cucamonga Wilderness is still required past the boundary (Forest Service). Icehouse Canyon parking guide Vincent Gap (Mt. Baden-Powell): approach from Wrightwood. No current Angeles closure order covers the lot, but we did not recheck its own status for this update. Caltrans lists Highway 2 closed from Islip Saddle to Vincent Gulch, so if you go, the way in is from the Big Pines side, not La Cañada. Vincent Gap parking guide Manker Flats and Devil's Punchbowl: neither appears in a current Angeles closure order. We did not recheck their own status pages for this update; see each guide for its last verified date.

sections.heading: What the Eaton Fire order closes
sections.body: Forest Order 05-01-26-04 was signed January 6, 2026 and runs from January 7, 2026 through December 31, 2027. It prohibits going onto National Forest land, roads or trails inside the closure area (signed order, PDF; closure map, PDF). The written boundary starts where the Mt. Wilson Trail meets the forest boundary above Sierra Madre, follows the forest boundary west, climbs the Chaney Trail and Mount Lowe Road (2N50) to the Mt. Wilson Road, runs east along that road to the Winter Creek Trail, and comes back down the Mt. Wilson Trail: the front range above Altadena, between the Chaney Trail and the Mt. Wilson Trail. Closed roads: Mount Wilson Toll Road below the Mt. Wilson Trail (2N45.2) and below Henninger Flats (2N45.3), and the Henninger Flats road (2N45B0). Closed trails: Idlehour, Castle Canyon, Sam Merrill lower, middle and upper, Echo Mountain, Mount Lowe West and Mount Lowe (East). The alert page also lists Idlehour and Millard trail camps as affected sites. Residents reaching private land, officials on duty and holders of a specific Forest Service exemption permit are exempt. Everyone else faces a fine of up to $5,000, up to six months in jail, or both. An order's end date is a ceiling, not a promise. The Forest Service can lift it early, shrink it or extend it, and when it lapses the trails don't automatically reopen. Watch the Angeles alerts page for a replacement order before planning a 2028 hike here.

sections.heading: Roads and the other Angeles closures
sections.body: Caltrans road information on the evening of October 17, 2026 (roads.dot.ca.gov, or call 1-800-427-7623): Highway 2 (Angeles Crest): closed from 3.3 miles east of Newcomb's Ranch to Islip Saddle, and from Islip Saddle to 5.4 miles west of Big Pines at Vincent Gulch, both for emergency repairs. Trailheads west of Newcomb's Ranch, including Switzer, are reached normally from La Cañada. Highway 39: closed from 2 miles north of Crystal Lake Road to Highway 2, around the clock, for construction. Three other Forest Service orders were in force when we checked: Williamson Rock, order 05-01-24-04: closes the Pacific Crest Trail from Highway 2 to the Burkhart Trail, plus the Williamson Rock area, to protect the endangered mountain yellow-legged frog. It runs through December 31, 2026 (alert). If no replacement order appears, check again before assuming it reopened on January 1. Rincon-Redbox Road (2N24.3), order 05-01-26-13: closed between Pine Mountain Road and Highway 39 after a rock slide, through December 31, 2026. The segment from Angeles Crest Highway to Pine Mountain is reachable with a free permit from the monument district office (alert). San Dimas Experimental Forest: closed to public recreation because it is a research forest.

sections.heading: Where the official sources disagree
sections.body: Mt. Wilson Trail from Sierra Madre. Not on the order's closed list, drawn as an open trail on the order's map, and listed as reopened by L.A. County, but listed as closed below Upper Winter Creek on the Forest Service's Chantry Flat page. We have not resolved this and won't guess. Mt. Wilson itself. The Chantry Flat page says Mt. Wilson "is in the post-Eaton Fire closure area." The order's map draws the closure's eastern edge along the Mt. Wilson Trail and shows the summit outside the hatched area. If the summit is your goal, ask the Los Angeles Gateway District, (818) 899-1900, which route it considers open. Millard Canyon is not a contradiction once both sources are read: L.A. County says Millard Canyon's trails are open while the campground stays closed, which matches the Forest Service listing Millard Trail Camp as an affected site.

sections.heading: Checking a trailhead yourself
sections.body:
Permission to be there, the road up, and the facility at the end are three separate facts, and each has its own source. For Forest Service land, read the alerts page and the order's map, then the site's own page, which carries an "open" or "closed" line near the top. Highways come from Caltrans. County parks such as Eaton Canyon and Devil's Punchbowl come from L.A. County Parks.

A hiking app marking a trail open is not evidence. Neither is an order disappearing from the alerts page: reopenings are announced, and an expired order is sometimes replaced weeks later.

faq.a: No. L.A. County lists Eaton Canyon Natural Area as closed until further notice due to the Eaton Fire, and its trails alert lists the Eaton Canyon Trail closed until December 31, 2027, as of October 17, 2026. The canyon above it, on national forest land, is inside Forest Order 05-01-26-04.

faq.q: When does the Eaton Fire closure end?
faq.a: Forest Order 05-01-26-04 runs through December 31, 2027. The Forest Service can end it earlier, change its boundary or extend it, so check the Angeles alerts page before relying on that date.

faq.q: Can I hike to Echo Mountain right now?
faq.a: No. The Sam Merrill Trail and the Echo Mountain Trail are both on the order's closed list through December 31, 2027, and entering carries a fine of up to $5,000 or up to six months in jail.

On October 17, 2026 the Forest Service listed Chantry Flat Picnic Area open from 6am to 8pm, along with First Water, Sturtevant, the Gabrielino Trail and the Winter Creek trails. The access road can close for safety separately, so check before driving up.

Only in part. On October 17, 2026 Caltrans listed Highway 2 closed from 3.3 miles east of Newcomb's Ranch to Vincent Gulch, west of Big Pines. The western section from La Cañada past Switzer was open.
